topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the lecture's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Pathogen and damage sensing via pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which the innate immune system detects pathogens and tissue damage using PAMPs, DAMPs, and various pattern recognition receptor pathways.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic inflammatory effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how sentinel cells initiate the acute inflammatory response, coordinate leukocyte extravasation into tissues, drain to lymph nodes, and potentially cause systemic pathologies like septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammatory outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the mechanisms required to terminate inflammation, repair damaged tissue, and manage long-term complications such as chronic inflammation and granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of the next topic
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and announces the subject of the next lecture.
